Prima Facie comprises evidence that is sufficient to prove a particular proposition or fact in the face of evidential rebuttal. It seeks to establish if there exists a solid legal case to answer following which proceedings may then commence to test it, and create a ruling. The result must be compelling enough for it to warrant trial.

An aim of the doctrine of prima facie is to prevent litigants from bringing spurious charges which simply waste all other parties' time. If they don't meet the threshold of the full weight of the burden of proof - by the evidence presented ... bye bye, don't waste our time.
